newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Neeman to be Israel's finance minister.
newsitem.headline: Neeman to be Israel's finance minister.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, hoping to quell a cabinet crisis, chose former justice minister Yaacov Neeman as Israel's new finance minister on Monday.

Cabinet minister Ariel Sharon had been tipped as the leading contender for the post, vacant since Netanyahu's party rival Dan Meridor resigned last month in a power struggle with the prime minister over foreign exchange policy.

Analysts said the Neeman appointment could help Netanyahu calm a crisis with Foreign Minister David Levy, who was apprehensive over hawkish ex-general Sharon was encroaching on his status as formal co-ordinator of peace talks
Levy had threatened to bolt and loss of his support would have left Netanyahu with a razor-thin majority in parliament.
The appointment was announced by Netanyahu's spokesman Shai Bazak who told Reuters: "Yaacov Neeman has agreed to the prime minister's request, and will be finance minister."
Israel Radio quoted Sharon as welcoming the appointment of Neeman, an attorney and former Treasury director-general.

Neeman served a brief stint as justice minister, but his indictment last August on charges of obstructing justice and lying under oath forced him to leave the job Netanyahu had given him less than two months earlier.

A court cleared Neeman of the charges in May, prompting speculation he might return to the justice post, filled by then-Likud legislator and Netanyahu loyalist Tzachi Hanegbi in what the prime minister originally termed a temporary appointment.
